title: Debate of the Chess Game
next_chapter_hook: Ye Qing's deep, dark eyes stared straight at him, her voice low and enchanting like a蛊: 'If... there was someone who could let you step outside this chessboard, would you dare to gamble?'

text.content: The night was as dark as ink, the cold wind carrying the dampness of the mountain. Chen Ji sat alone at the edge of the cliff, the jade slip in his hand already white-knuckled from his grip. The words on the jade slip burned like a brand into his mind—'The Chen bloodline, generation after generation, all are chess pieces.' Had his struggles and scheming all these years never escaped beyond the chessboard? Rage burned in his chest like wildfire, shaking his very vitals.

dialogue.content: 'You sit here alone—are you planning to jump, or waiting for someone?' Ye Qing's voice drifted from the darkness, tinged with mockery. She walked closer, the aura of the Holy Sect's demon path faintly visible in the night. 'The fluctuations from the Tianji Record are intense. What happened?'

text.content: Chen Ji raised his head, the fire of rage still not extinguished in his eyes, but he forced it down, leaving only an abyss of cold intent. He handed the jade slip to Ye Qing, his voice terrifyingly calm: 'Look at this.' Ye Qing took the jade slip, and the moment her spiritual sense entered it, her pupils constricted sharply—that line of text, she saw it clearly.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji decided to show Ye Qing more truths from the Tianji Record, but he needed to decide how much to reveal.

choices.description: Let Ye Qing see all records of the Chen family's fate within the Tianji Record, including the deliberately hidden truths.
choices.visible_reward: Gain Ye Qing's deeper understanding and possible assistance
choices.risk_hint: Ye Qing might learn too much, becoming an unstable factor

text.content: Chen Ji took a deep breath, taking out the Tianji Record Fragment. A vision of light and shadow slowly unfolded between them—those were images of the Chen ancestors through generations. They struggled, rebelled, submitted, and in the end, all fell at the same destination. Ye Qing's breathing grew rapid.

choices.description: Only let Ye Qing see the part about 'chess pieces,' keeping other key information as hidden trump cards.
choices.visible_cost: Ye Qing might feel there are reservations
choices.visible_reward: Maintain information superiority, not fully exposing trump cards
choices.risk_hint: Ye Qing might develop doubts because of this

text.content: Chen Ji narrowed his eyes slightly, only passing the passage from the jade slip to Ye Qing via spiritual sense. The vision flashed briefly, and he stopped in time, only showing her the tip of the iceberg. Ye Qing frowned slightly, seemingly dissatisfied.

dialogue.content: After Ye Qing finished reading, she fell silent for a long while. When she spoke again, her voice carried a gravity Chen Ji had never heard before: 'Generation after generation as chess pieces... do you know what that means?' She raised her head, those dark eyes flashing with complex light: 'It means the hand controlling you is far larger than you imagined.'

Chen Ji let out a cold laugh, the smile full of self-mockery: 'I thought I was the one playing the game, turns out I was just being self-righteous on someone else's chessboard.' His hand slowly clenched, fingernails digging deep into his palms, blood seeping through his fingers. 'Ridiculous, utterly ridiculous!'

'Ridiculous?' Ye Qing suddenly laughed softly, that smile carrying an indefinable meaning: 'Chen Ji, do you know who the Demon Path Commander is?' She paused, voice dropping to an extreme whisper. 'He is also one of the 'Twin Ones'—like you, a chess piece selected by fate.'

choice.prompt: The Demon Path Commander is also a chess piece of fate? This information was too shocking, and Chen Ji needed to decide how to respond.

choices.text: Inquire About the Twin Ones Details
choices.description: Deeply question Ye Qing about the 'Twin Ones,' trying to piece together more truth.
choices.visible_reward: Gain more clues about the fate chess game

text.content: Chen Ji's eyes flashed with sharp light: 'Twin Ones? How much do you know?' Sensing the urgency in his words, Ye Qing's lips curved slightly upward: 'Why the rush? This secret... I can trade it for one promise from you.'

choices.description: Suppress the shock within, probe Ye Qing's knowledge from a bystander's perspective.
choices.visible_cost: May miss the chance to learn more deeply
choices.visible_reward: Maintain negotiation initiative, not exposing trump cards
choices.risk_hint: Ye Qing might not reveal anything more because of this

text.content: Chen Ji suppressed his rage, his expression反而calm下来. He looked at Ye Qing with a half-smile: 'You know quite a lot. But... why would the Holy Sect's Saint tell me all this?' Those eyes seemed to say: I know you have motives.

Ye Qing laughed softly, that smile carrying a hint of bitterness: 'Because we're all chess pieces, aren't we?' She extended her hand, and in the moonlight that hand was fair as jade, yet faint blue veins were visible. 'You think the Holy Sect controls me with poison? No, it's with 'life'—my life hasn't been my own for a long time.'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji fell silent. Ye Qing's words were like a sharp blade, dissecting the truth he had been evading. He slowly stood up, gazing toward the distant Tianqing Sect, voice hoarse: 'I once thought, as long as I was clever enough, patient enough, I could escape this chess game.' He forced a bitter smile. 'Turns out, from the beginning, there was never a distinction between inside and outside the chessboard.'

text.content: 'But there's one thing you haven't figured out.' Ye Qing walked closer to him, her voice low. 'Since we're all chess pieces, why is it that you specifically got the Tianji Record? Why is it that I can understand that prophecy?' Her eyes sparkled with extraordinary light under the moonlight. 'This itself... isn't it a kind of possibility?'

choice.prompt: Ye Qing's words gave Chen Ji a glimpse of a possibility to break the game, but this possibility was filled with unknowns.

choices.description: Since fate gave them the special identity of chess pieces, perhaps it was precisely for them to break the chess game.
choices.visible_cost: Might be fooled by fate again
choices.visible_reward: Gain a theoretical possibility for breaking free
choices.risk_hint: Might be an even deeper trap

dialogue.content: Chen Ji turned around, staring straight into Ye Qing's eyes: 'You mean... we chess pieces might have been variables planted by the chessboard itself?' His voice trembled slightly, whether from excitement or fear. 'If that's truly the case, then let me see—what game is this chessboard trying to play!'

choices.description: This idea is too optimistic, one cannot easily believe in so-called 'possibilities.'
choices.visible_cost: Might miss the real chance to break free
choices.visible_reward: Maintain rationality,不被虚假的希望迷惑

text.content: Chen Ji did not respond immediately, falling into deep contemplation. After a moment, he shook his head: 'This feels too much like a trap. If fate truly has a will, why would it give chess pieces the possibility to break free?' His tone was ice-cold: 'Unless... this is exactly what it wants.'

Hearing this, Ye Qing did not get angry; instead, she laughed. That laughter was especially clear in the silent night, yet carried a trace of desolation: 'You're right, Chen Ji.' Her gaze deepened. 'But have you considered—if even doubt is designed, then does it matter whether you doubt or not?'

dialogue.content: 'So...' Ye Qing's voice suddenly dropped, carrying an unprecedented seriousness: 'Instead of passively waiting to die, why not proactively charge forward? Even if we crash and bleed... at least—' She paused. 'At least it proves we're still alive.'

text.content: Chen Ji fell silent. Looking at this Holy Sect Saint before him, he suddenly felt a similarity—she was like him, a chess piece caught in fate's grip, yet unwilling to be a piece to be manipulated. The night wind blew, rustling their robes. After a long while, Chen Ji spoke: 'Tell me, what exactly do you want to do?'

dialogue.content: A flash of惊喜 appeared in Ye Qing's eyes, then quickly faded to calm. She took a deep breath, producing from her sleeve a pitch-black token, on it carved a twisted rune: 'This is the core of my Holy Sect's forbidden formation. If you can break it...' Her voice dropped to an extreme whisper. 'It can sever fate's control over some chess pieces. And Mo Xiansheng in your Tianji Record might know the remaining key.'

text.content: Chen Ji stared at the token, his pupils constricting. He understood its weight—Ye Qing was wagering her own life. 'Aren't you afraid I'll take the token and then betray you?' Chen Ji asked gravely. Ye Qing laughed instead, that smile carrying a sense of relief: 'I am afraid. But compared to continuing as a chess piece... I want to see what scenery lies beyond the shattered chessboard.'

Chen Ji reached out, and the moment his fingertip touched the token, a cold aura rushed along his meridians straight to his heart. He saw countless points of light—those were threads of fate, connecting all living beings under heaven. And among those points of light, one thread was exceptionally dazzling, connecting in two directions: one was him, and the other... was a blurred figure. That figure's outline strongly resembled his long-missing sister—Chen Nian.

'Chen Nian...' Chen Ji murmured, his voice trembling slightly. That thread was so fragile, as if it might break at any moment, yet tenaciously connected the two ends of fate. Sensing his strange reaction, Ye Qing frowned: 'What did you see?' Chen Ji did not answer, only gripping the token tightly, his knuckles white from the force.

dialogue.content: Ye Qing's deep, dark eyes stared straight at him, her voice low and enchanting: 'If... there was someone who could let you step outside this chessboard, would you dare to gamble?' The night wind suddenly rose, scattering the last distance between them. In the distance, the lights of Tianqing Sect glowed dimly, and further away, the horns of the demon army's advance were already faintly audible. Chen Ji gripped the token tightly, his eyes flashing with complex light—rage,不甘, and a flicker of hope that had never been extinguished.
